maya.activity: Wake beside Daniel, stretch quietly, check his face and temperature if he agrees, and ask only how he is feeling before getting dressed.
maya.intention: Start gently and notice whether his symptoms have changed without making him manage the morning.

maya.activity: Make ginger tea and a small breakfast for myself, carry tea and water to Daniel, and leave toast and fruit within easy reach without insisting he eat.
maya.intention: Keep both of us fed and hydrated while leaving Daniel free to rest.

maya.activity: Check the bedroom and living room quietly, put Daniel's phone and water where he can reach them, and gather only obvious dishes into the kitchen.
maya.intention: Make the shared spaces practical without turning the morning into a full cleaning project.

maya.activity: Make a slow, simple breakfast for myself and plan the coming week at the dining table, keeping easy food available for Daniel and leaving the counters clear.
maya.intention: Follow the Sunday routine in a gentler form and make the week feel manageable.

maya.activity: Wash the breakfast dishes, wipe the kitchen counter and sink area, and put the reusable grocery bags away after checking that they are dry.
maya.intention: Reset the kitchen while I have enough energy, without disturbing Daniel's rest.

maya.activity: Make tomato soup and toast, carry a bowl and water to Daniel if he wants them, and eat at the kitchen counter myself.
maya.intention: Provide a warm, low-effort lunch and avoid asking Daniel to choose or prepare anything.

maya.activity: Wash the saucepan, bowl, and spoon, put any remaining soup into the leftover container, and lower the living-room lights before checking on Daniel.
maya.intention: Keep the afternoon calm and make rest easier for him.

maya.activity: Sit nearby while Daniel rests, read quietly, and refresh his tea or water without expecting conversation.
maya.intention: Be present and attentive during the time he would usually be out, while letting him set the pace.

maya.activity: At the glass desk, review the week's notes and gather personal papers into a short, orderly stack before calling my mother.
maya.intention: Prepare for the usual afternoon call without letting household worry expand into unnecessary work.

maya.activity: Call my mother and sort personal papers at the glass desk, pausing to check Daniel's face if he comes within view or needs anything.
maya.intention: Keep the usual connection with my mother while remaining available to Daniel.

maya.activity: Check Daniel's symptoms, refresh his tea and water, and write a brief note about his temperature, appetite, and medication timing if needed.
maya.intention: Track the third day of illness clearly and notice whether medical advice may be necessary.

maya.activity: Make a very simple dinner, carry Daniel a small portion only if he wants it, and eat at the kitchen counter.
maya.intention: Offer food without making dinner an event or requiring him to decide much.

maya.activity: Wash dinner dishes, store leftovers, wipe the stovetop and counters, and leave a mug and water ready for later.
maya.intention: Finish the necessary kitchen work before settling in for the evening.

maya.activity: Sit with Daniel on the sectional while he rests, read quietly, and keep the remote and tissues within reach.
maya.intention: Offer company without assuming he is well enough for the usual film.

maya.activity: Ask softly whether Daniel wants a short, quiet film or simply the lights low; follow the easier option and stay beside him without pressing for conversation.
maya.intention: Keep the usual evening shape but let his condition determine whether entertainment is manageable.

maya.activity: Clear the coffee table into small destination piles, check Daniel's water and phone, and make a final brief note if his symptoms changed.
maya.intention: Restore enough order for morning and keep essentials close to him.

maya.activity: Wash up, change into sleepwear, put my phone on charge, and leave my reading glasses in the upper nightstand drawer.
maya.intention: Prepare for sleep without creating extra decisions or noise.

maya.activity: Get into bed beside Daniel, keep water within reach, and settle quietly without asking him to make any decisions.
maya.intention: End the day simply and remain available overnight.

daniel.activity: Wake in bedroom 1, check how Maya slept and how she is feeling, then bring her water and make sure her phone, tissues, and anything else she needs are within reach. I keep the room quiet before showering and dressing.
daniel.intention: Start the day with a calm symptom check and make rest easy for Maya.

daniel.activity: Make coffee and a mild breakfast in the kitchen. I grind the beans by hand, carry my mug from the bar cabinet area to the counter, prepare a small portion for myself, and make tea and simple food for Maya if she wants it. I leave the tasting spoon on the sink side.
daniel.intention: Provide gentle food and fluids without asking Maya to cook or plan breakfast.

daniel.activity: Eat at the kitchen counter, clear the most visible breakfast items, and carry Maya’s tea or water upstairs if she is resting. I check her temperature and symptoms, keeping my phone on the bar cart while I move between the counter and bedroom.
daniel.intention: Keep breakfast manageable and remain available while Maya rests.

daniel.activity: Make a small saucepan of plain broth and prepare easy fruit and snacks. I carry a bowl and water to Maya, then wash the saucepan and leave the tasting spoon on the open sink side instead of starting a full cleanup.
daniel.intention: Set up nourishing, low-effort food for the next few hours.

daniel.activity: Eat a light lunch at the counter, refill my water bottle, and do a quiet check-in with Maya. I collect only the obvious dishes so I can stay nearby without hovering.
daniel.intention: Eat enough to stay useful and preserve a calm atmosphere.

daniel.activity: Do a short essential work block in bedroom 2 with the laptop on its stand and a written priority list. I keep the door open and pause once to check whether Maya needs water, broth, or medicine.
daniel.intention: Handle only necessary work while keeping caregiving interruptions easy.

daniel.activity: Make a short grocery run for broth ingredients, fruit, tea, and other easy food, then return directly home rather than taking the usual walk or browsing records. I carry the reusable grocery bag and keep my phone with me.
daniel.intention: Restock essentials without turning the errand into a tiring outing.

daniel.activity: Put away the groceries, refresh the broth, and bring a small snack and water to Maya. I check her temperature and symptoms again, then sit quietly nearby if she is awake and leave her undisturbed if she is sleeping.
daniel.intention: Restore supplies and support an afternoon rest period.

daniel.activity: Do another brief work block in bedroom 2, stopping early if Maya calls. I keep the laptop setup compact and write down anything that can wait until tomorrow.
daniel.intention: Complete essential work without letting it compete with Maya’s recovery.

daniel.activity: Prepare a simple early dinner with extra broth, carrying bowls to the dining table. I bring Maya a manageable portion and water wherever she is resting, then eat my own portion at the table.
daniel.intention: Make dinner easy to tolerate and avoid creating another task for Maya.

daniel.activity: Clear the most visible dinner items, wash the essential dishes, and check Maya’s temperature and symptoms once more. I make tea if she wants it and keep the lights low.
daniel.intention: Leave the main surfaces usable while staying focused on evening comfort.

daniel.activity: Sit on the sectional with water and a quiet book, remaining available for a check-in. If Maya feels up to it, I can put on a low-volume film, but I do not make the evening depend on that; I leave the phone on the bar cart until I notice it.
daniel.intention: Offer companionship without pressuring Maya into the usual film routine.

daniel.activity: Wash up, brush my teeth, change into sleepwear, and carry a fresh glass of water into bedroom 1. I put anything Maya may need close to the bed and make the room comfortable for another difficult night.
daniel.intention: Prepare the bedroom for rest and make overnight help straightforward.

daniel.activity: Get into the king bed, keep the lights and conversation low, and listen for Maya without repeatedly waking her. I leave my phone within reach and focus on resting so I can help again tomorrow.
daniel.intention: Rest while remaining quietly attentive overnight.
